hints: Write down, for each position, which position its reading has to end up in. What kind of object is that?
It is a permutation, and every permutation splits into cycles: a reading goes here, whatever was here goes there, and eventually you come back to where you started.
A cycle of length `L` needs exactly `L - 1` swaps, and cycles never interfere with one another. So the answer is `n` minus the number of cycles.
Build the permutation by sorting the positions by their readings, then walk it marking what you have visited; each unvisited start opens a new cycle.
